plan: [I have value $24. With the common-component structure, a high own value signals others may also have high values (winner’s curse). In a second-price auction it’s sensible to shade my bid below my full value to avoid overpaying while still winning when I truly have the highest value. I pick a modest shading of $2 to trade off win probability and expected surplus.]

[This is a sealed-bid second-price auction. In independent-private-value settings truth-telling (bid = value) is dominant; with affiliated signals there is winner's-curse risk, but with no history and one round the safest profit-maximizing action is to bid my true valuation. My private value is $32, bids in $0.1 increments, so I'll bid $32 exactly to capture positive surplus when I win.]

[This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction. In such auctions bidding your true private value is the safest strategy: underbidding risks losing profitable wins, overbidding risks paying more than the prize is worth. We have no prior rounds to update beliefs. Even with the common-value component, a truthful bid of $44 avoids negative-profit outcomes and maximizes expected payoff in this one-shot setting.]
